messages.subject: Float Truncation Problem when Parsing JSON
messages.subject_clean: Float Truncation Problem when Parsing JSON
messages.body_plain:
Hi,


I am currently programming my own small R IDE running on a Java Server and
am thus using JRI.
The problem I have right now is, that if I try to parse JSON from my R
session, the floats get truncated.

For example this code:


rjson::fromJSON('3.7')


is evaluated to: [REAL* (3.0)]


I checked the exact same code with my normal R installation, and I get
the correct answer of 3.7.


I also tried another R JSON library called jsonlite, but get exactly
the same output.


Do you have any idea, what is happening here?



Best regards,

Artjom

messages.subject: Re: Float Truncation Problem when Parsing JSON
messages.subject_clean: Float Truncation Problem when Parsing JSON
messages.body_plain:
Artjom,

this is typically a locale issue - you are likely running in a LC_NUMERIC locale that doesn't use dot (.) as the decimals separator - compare Sys.getlocale() in your R session and in your Java session. Try setting LC_NUMERIC to something more sane, R typically enforces LC_NUMERIC=C, but since you run it from Java it is Java setting the locale.

To illustrate in R:

> Sys.setlocale("LC_NUMERIC","de_DE.UTF-8")
[1] "de_DE.UTF-8"
Warning message:
In Sys.setlocale("LC_NUMERIC", "de_DE.UTF-8") :
  setting 'LC_NUMERIC' may cause R to function strangely
> rjson::fromJSON('3.7')
[1] 3
> Sys.setlocale("LC_NUMERIC","C")
[1] "C"
> rjson::fromJSON('3.7')
[1] 3.7

and as you can see R is explicitly warning about such locales since they break a lot of things.

Cheers,
Simon
